skill.name: ai-avatar-video
skill.description: Create talking head and AI avatar videos with inference.sh models. Generate speech, animate portraits, create lip sync, localize videos, and produce presenter content.
skill.summary: Build avatar video workflows from portraits, scripts, audio, or existing video.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, placeholder media URLs, or ordinary documentation links. Confirmed findings concern unpinned skill installation and mutable remote installation guidance. The workflows also send potentially biometric media to third-party processing and can incur paid service usage.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation commands use unpinned community sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each skill dependency to a reviewed immutable commit or release, and require user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: CLI installation guidance is loaded from a mutable branch.
remediation.suggestion: Link to an immutable commit and include the required installation steps directly for review.

remediation.issue: Avatar workflows transfer portraits, voices, and videos to external model services.
remediation.suggestion: Require consent before upload and warn users not to submit confidential media or media without appropriate rights.

remediation.issue: Remote model commands can consume paid inference credits.
remediation.suggestion: Show the selected model and estimated job count, then obtain confirmation before starting paid or batch runs.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar and Talking Head Videos
content.value_statement: Producing presenter videos requires coordinated image, speech, and lip sync tools. This skill builds inference.sh workflows for avatars, localization, and batch content.
actual_capabilities: Creates talking head videos from a portrait and written script.
Animates portraits with user-provided audio for lip sync.
Combines portrait generation, speech generation, and avatar rendering.
Builds transcription, translation, speech, and lip sync workflows for dubbing.
Generates multiple presenter variants with fixed voice and style settings.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, network access, and available credits.
Uploads media references and prompts to third-party model services.
Output quality depends on source portrait lighting, framing, and audio clarity.
Model availability, prices, voices, languages, and performance can change.

use_cases.title: Produce Product Presenters
use_cases.description: Create scripted presenter videos for product demos, announcements, and short advertisements.

use_cases.title: Localize Existing Videos
use_cases.description: Transcribe, translate, synthesize speech, and synchronize a video for another language.

use_cases.title: Animate Course Material
use_cases.description: Turn lesson scripts and approved portraits into consistent educational presenter clips.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 720p talking head video from my portrait and script. Use a natural English voice and show the planned model before running it.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first-time user needs one simple presenter video.

prompt_templates.title: Match a Presenter Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a vertical avatar video with a calm professional voice, restrained gestures, and a neutral office background. Use my approved portrait and script.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a presenter that follows brand direction.

prompt_templates.title: Localize a Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe my video, translate the speech into Spanish, generate matching audio, and lip sync the original. Pause for approval before each paid stage.
prompt_templates.scenario: A localization specialist needs a reviewed multilingual workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Presenter Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three presenter variants for this campaign. Compare suitable models, estimate job count and cost, confirm media rights, then run only my approved variants.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs controlled batch production.

output_examples.input: Create a short welcome video from an approved portrait and a 40-word script.
output: Selected workflow: P-Video-Avatar with built-in speech.
Format: 720p, portrait aspect ratio, natural English voice.
Approval required before one paid remote generation job.

output_examples.input: Dub a training video into Spanish.
output: Stage 3: generate approved speech and synchronize the video.

output_examples.input: Create three vertical presenter variations for a product campaign.
output_examples.output: Prepared three presenter variants with distinct approved voices, consistent 1080p framing, and a three-job cost confirmation.

best_practices: Obtain consent and usage rights for every face, voice, script, and source video.
Review the selected model, media destination, job count, and estimated cost before execution.
Use front-facing portraits with clear lighting and clean audio for stable lip sync.
anti_patterns: Do not upload confidential, biometric, or licensed media without authorization.
Do not install unpinned skills or follow mutable remote instructions without review.
Do not launch paid batch jobs before the user approves scope and expected charges.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, network access, and sufficient service credits.

faq.question: Can it create speech from text?
faq.answer: Yes. P-Video-Avatar includes speech generation, and separate speech models support workflows with other avatar models.

faq.question: Can it use my own audio?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported workflows can animate a portrait or synchronize a video with an approved audio source.

faq.question: Can it localize existing videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines transcription, translation, speech generation, and lip sync stages for multilingual video.

faq.question: Where is my media processed?
faq.answer: The examples send media references and prompts to remote inference.sh model apps for processing.

faq.question: Does generation cost money?
faq.answer: Remote models can consume paid credits. Review current pricing and confirm the job count before execution.
